messages:
maya: FYI alert — dedicated capacity in eu-north is showing sustained queue growth and increased admission 429s for burstable tenants. seeing token_queue_size jump and headroom depletion. starting triage.
alex: where are the 429s coming from (committed vs burst)? link to dashboard?
jon: most of the 429s are for tier=standard and tier=burstable. committed tenants still mostly served but their p95 has crept up. quick metrics: queue_depth=1240, admission_rate=78r/s, drop_rate=12r/s :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maya: thanks. I think a nightly internal loadtest kicked off a bulk rerun plus one external partner retried a large job. checking job origins.
sre-bot: Incident alert — eu-north-dedicated-pool: admission-controller detected sustained saturation > 10m, auto-shed policy applied (policy:burst-priority->low).
tara: @maya can we temporarily raise committed tenant weight? we're seeing SLO risk for a few key customers.
maya: yes planning to bump fairshare weights for committed tenants and enable the short burst buffer for 10m. doing it now.
ryan: note: bumping fairshare will push more pressure onto provisioning; if underlying node drain/oz imbalance exists we might still see evictions. check node alloc.
alex: running quick k8s snapshot:```kubectl get pods -n dedicated-eun -o wide | grep gpu``` shows a couple of pending pods on node-az3 and node-az1, and one node draining due to maintenance.
jon: logs from admission-controller: `WARN admission: pool eu-north saturated, applying token-backpressure to tenant=burstable, tokens_per_sec=0.5`
ops-oncall: rolling back a noisy internal job now (id: lt-2026-03-18-xx). paused in CI.
maya: ps: adding an override rule to limit internal test job concurrency to 10 across the pool. also enabling temporary routing rule to divert new burstable requests to hosted tier for 20m.
tara: can we also increase the admission cap for committed tenants from 300->420 r/s? that's a big jump — we should measure if that causes further queueing.
maya: increasing to 380 r/s for now (delta small). monitoring.
jon: after the weight bump and routing, queue_depth down to 420, drop_rate -> 3r/s, p95 latency for committed back to baseline.
sre-bot: Auto-mitigation: temporary burst buffer enabled (10m), fairshare overrides applied for tenants marked committed.
ryan: good short-term fix. we should follow up: 1) reduce single-tenant burst limits for non-production keys, 2) schedule nightly loadtest to isolated test pool, 3) add automated detection when a single origin consumes >40% of pool for >5m.
ops-oncall: filing follow-up ticket in backlog and tagging eng-sre for postmortem.
maya: action items: triage done. I'll own the postmortem and a config change PR to add origin-based throttles + a flag to auto-divert burstable to hosted when pool saturation > 70%.
alex: also recommend a small cost note: dedicated surge buffer means extra credits; will estimate in PR.
jon: quick sanity: please capture the admission-controller metrics and the k8s node events for the 30m window starting at 1799994200.
maya: copied. I'll post the draft postmortem link here when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
